prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-03-19, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-03-19):
| Current ratio           | 1.34 |
| Retained earnings       | 22,804M |
| Current liabilities     | 20,957M |
| Current assets          | 28,007M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 31,211M |
| Total liabilities       | 34,289M |
| Total assets            | 67,064M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,494M |
| Revenue                 | 18,044M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid liquidity (current ratio 1.34; current assets exceed current liabilities) and positive earnings (EBIT 2,494M on 18,044M revenue) with a reasonable equity cushion. However, total liabilities are sizable relative to assets (liabilities ~34,289M of 67,064M) indicating moderate leverage and potential sensitivity to earnings volatility. On balance, the credit risk appears stable but not strongly premium, supporting a BBB rating.

DECISION: BBB
